tables.title: Actual Values Used in Simulations.
notes: Table 2 lists actual values used in simulations for two paths.
In DCS-SOMP case, q_az and q_el are both set to 18; in adaptive DCS-SOMP scenario, q_az and q_el are both set to 6.

observations: Figures 4a–4b display the comparison between DCS-SOMP and adaptive DCS-SOMP for 2D-AoD, 2D-AoA, and ToA.
The results correspond to a random run for Path 1.

For all cases, the adaptive DCS-SOMP significantly enhances the estimation of the respective angle as early as the second iteration, gradually converging towards the actual value with each subsequent iteration.

Figure 4 caption: Comparison of (a) Azimuth AoD estimation and (b) Elevation AoD estimation results using DCS-SOMP and adaptive DCS-SOMP. The outcomes pertain to Path 1. In the DCS-SOMP case, q_az and q_el are both set to 18, whereas in the adaptive DCS-SOMP scenario, q_az and q_el are both set to 6.
uncertainties: The text states 'arbitrary actual values' were selected for two paths as described in Table 2, but does not specify how randomness or selection criteria were applied beyond the stated settings.
The threshold for iteration stopping is given as ρ = 10⁻⁶, but no explicit confirmation is provided that this exact threshold was met in all runs shown in Figures 4a–4b.
Figure 4 plots show convergence behavior but do not provide raw numerical iteration-by-iteration output values; only visual trends are presented.
